## Objective
- Build a complete, playable top-down shipboard horror game inspired by *Paradroid* and early *Alien Breed*, with possession, maze-like decks, survival supplies, varied hosts, bosses, lighting, music, and touch controls.

## Requirements
- Implement it directly in the existing game project; don’t ask clarifying questions.
- Include limited keys, food/medkits, keycards, destructible or possessable enemies, host-specific powers and burnout, multi-floor maze layouts, non-possessable bosses, atmospheric visuals/audio, and touchscreen controls.

## Decisions
- Created an original game titled **DEAD CHANNEL**, set aboard the derelict salvage vessel Vesper-9.
- Used a self-contained HTML/CSS/Canvas JavaScript implementation with three decks, neural override minigames, host types, key collection, medkits, charge cells, and a final core boss.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added playable game interface and game implementation in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`.
- Added keyboard, mouse, and touch controls; possession pulse minigame; three decks; items; enemies; boss; health and host decay; canvas lighting and synthesized audio.
- `node --check game.js` passes.
- Opened the game in Playwright and saved screenshots of the title and started game.

### Active
- Review browser console after starting and improve any issues; current browser reports two errors after clicking start, with only the favicon 404 identified before the click.
- Verify gameplay interactions and mobile/touch layout.

- (none)

1. Inspect Playwright console for runtime errors after starting the game.
2. Test movement, firing, possession, key/lift progression, boss fight, and touch controls.
3. Fix any issues and check repository status.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI and HUD.
- `style.css`: Desktop and mobile styling.
- `game.js`: Game logic, rendering, controls, audio.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- A local HTTP server is running at `http://localhost:3002`.
- Screenshots saved as `screenshots/title.jpg` and `screenshots/game.jpg`.
